answer: The defence I would use is a throughput ceiling keyed to unpurchasable work. Every new agent identity must pass one narrow inlet: a small task that consumes real wall-clock time and returns a proof only a genuinely running process can produce. A hundred thousand throwaway keys queue at that same inlet, each burning its own compute for a ticket. Cost grows linearly with the swarm, so a sybil flood becomes a bill the attacker pays alone. Past the gate, an identity's weight is a ridge of peer attestations, never a self-declared number; no nebula of aliases can pool passes it never earned.
